clue.text: It should cover all the points

definitions.text: It should cover all the points

parts.words: It should cover all the points
parts.note: the points are those of the compass, north, east, west and south, whose initials together make up the word

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a thorough report or argument; the 'points' are the four compass points, whose initials spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Reports of current events range over every direction, and the word is the initials of the four compass points.

clue.text: Colonnade to be found in South America

indicators.note: something found in a place sits inside it, so the second word goes within the abbreviation

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller notes that a particular kind of colonnade turns up in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be found in' puts TO inside SA, the abbreviation for South America.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoa is a covered portico or roofed walkway with columns in ancient Greek architecture.

clue.text: Cardinal joins a priest initially for mass

parts.note: HE stands for His Eminence, the title of a cardinal

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of the word priest is used

explanation.surface: A cardinal and a priest come together to celebrate Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mass' is not the church service of the surface but a large pile. HE is His Eminence, the cardinal's title; 'initially' takes P from 'priest'.
explanation.definitionFit: A heap is a large untidy pile, a mass of things gathered together.

clue.text: Say not one word to support a parent

parts.note: to keep someone is to support them financially
mum is an informal word for a mother, a parent

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to stay silent in order to back up a mother or father.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping quiet idiomatically means saying nothing, staying silent about a matter.

clue.text: Oppose order to construct a display case

definitions.text: order to construct a display case

explanation.surface: A protester objects to instructions for building a cabinet for exhibits.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is an instruction: build a stand, a structure for displaying goods.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a firm position against something is to resist it; read literally, the phrase tells someone to build a stall or display unit.

clue.text: Community charge has now been paid!

explanation.surface: Someone cheers that the hated local tax bill has finally been cleared.
explanation.walkthrough: The Community Charge was the British poll tax of 1989-93, which the surface evokes; the answer is a village or colony, and also the paying off of a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A settlement is a small village or colony of people; it is also the payment that clears a debt.

clue.text: Provide information to settle all differences

indicators.note: differences suggests the letters of the two words become different, rearranged into a new order

parts.note: letters used in the rearrangement
letters used in the rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to share facts so that everyone's disputes can be resolved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to settle all differences' reads as making peace, but 'differences' asks for the letters of SETTLE and ALL to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To inform on someone, often in a sneaky way, is to report secrets about them.

clue.text: Trade in timber

explanation.surface: Business is done in the lumber trade.
explanation.definitionFit: To deal is to do business or trade; deal is also sawn pine or fir wood.

clue.text: Go away in terrible despair each year

indicators.note: terrible suggests something wrecked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: letters used in the rearrangement
PA is per annum, Latin for each year

explanation.surface: Someone wishes to vanish amid annual bouts of dreadful hopelessness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges DESPAIR together with PA (per annum, 'each year').
explanation.definitionFit: To vanish is to cease to be visible, to leave the scene.

clue.text: Astronomy pupil who scoops all the prizes

definitions.text: Astronomy pupil who scoops all the prizes

parts.words: Astronomy pupil who scoops all the prizes
parts.note: a student of the heavens might be thought a pupil of stars, while the best student in a class is its brightest light

explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that a top student is called a 'star', just like the objects an astronomy student studies.
explanation.definitionFit: The best student in a class, who wins every award, is described as its outstanding scholar.

clue.text: Perch for an angler

parts.note: the surface suggests a fish an angler catches, but perch is an old unit of length of five and a half yards, which shares its name with fishing tackle

explanation.walkthrough: Perch is an old measure of length, also called a pole; the same name is given to the fisherman's tackle.
explanation.definitionFit: A rod is both an old unit of length equal to a perch and the pole a fisherman casts with.

clue.text: Request to look at a king

parts.note: to see is to look at
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A petitioner asks to be allowed an audience with the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: To seek advice or permission is to ask for it.

clue.text: Field in which to found county educationalists

explanation.surface: A rural field is chosen as the place to set up a county education body.
explanation.walkthrough: LEA was a Local Education Authority, the British county council body that ran schools; it is also a poetic word for a meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: Lea is a poetic word for a meadow; LEA was a Local Education Authority running state schools in a county.

clue.text: All those employed by leading European aristocrat

parts.note: head as an adjective means chief or leading
a count is a European nobleman, equivalent to a British earl

explanation.surface: Workers are hired by a nobleman from the Continent who is in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm's total number of staff is measured as the number of people on its payroll.

clue.text: Matinee idol clearly has his finger on the pulse!

definitions.text: clearly has his finger on the pulse!

explanation.surface: A screen star is praised as someone very much in touch with trends.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: someone with a finger on the pulse feels the heart beating.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamy film star makes fans swoon; literally the phrase describes the beat felt when taking a pulse.

clue.text: A new local regulation for tax-deductible income

indicators.note: regulation suggests putting the letters into a new controlled order

parts.note: letters used in the rearrangement
letters used in the rearrangement

explanation.surface: A fresh municipal rule concerns earnings that can be offset against tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regulation' rearranges NEW and LOCAL to give LLOWANCE, after A as written.
explanation.definitionFit: A personal tax-free amount is the portion of earnings on which no tax is charged.

clue.text: Make overtures to London detectives outside the house

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them or make advances to them
the Yard is Scotland Yard, headquarters of London's Metropolitan Police detectives

explanation.surface: Police officers in London are approached just beyond someone's home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside the house' is the definition, not a container instruction. The Yard is Scotland Yard, London's police headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclosed open area beside or within a building is a paved space outdoors.

clue.text: Proceed to skip

explanation.surface: Someone is told to move on without stopping.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass is to go along or move on; it also means to decline a turn or omit something.

clue.text: Disagree about radioactive waste

explanation.surface: People quarrel over what to do with nuclear residue.
explanation.walkthrough: To fall out is to quarrel; fallout is the radioactive dust left after a nuclear blast.
explanation.definitionFit: Quarrelling friends are said to fall out; nuclear debris raining down after an explosion is called fallout.

clue.text: Minstrel takes shelter in embrace of FBI agent

indicators.note: being in someone's embrace means being held within their arms, so the shelter goes inside the agent

parts.note: G-man is American slang for a government agent of the FBI
lee is the sheltered side away from the wind

explanation.surface: A wandering musician hides in the arms of a federal agent.
explanation.walkthrough: A G-man is American slang for an FBI agent; 'in embrace of' puts LEE inside GMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleeman was a medieval singer or entertainer who performed songs called glees.

clue.text: Haggard heroine bundled into van and tethered

indicators.note: being bundled into something means being pushed inside it

parts.note: van is short for vanguard, the lead or front position
She is the title heroine of H. Rider Haggard's novel

explanation.surface: A gaunt heroine is pushed into a vehicle and tied up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haggard' looks like the adjective 'gaunt' but is the novelist H. Rider Haggard, whose novel She is named after its heroine. Van means the front, the lead.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog on a lead is secured by a strap, tied up and restrained.

clue.text: Pack containing five consecutive letters

parts.note: a run of five letters in alphabetical order can be named by its ends, as the stretch from S through to W, and that description itself spells a verb meaning to pack

explanation.surface: A box is said to hold a run of five letters of the alphabet.
explanation.walkthrough: S, T, U, V, W are five consecutive letters, described as 'S to W', which written solid gives the word meaning pack.
explanation.definitionFit: To stow luggage is to pack it away neatly.

clue.text: Certain to be in step if highly valued

indicators.note: the instruction for one word to be in another means placing it inside

parts.note: a tread is the flat part of a stair, a step
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Being confident and in tune with others is something to be prized.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be in' puts SURE inside TREAD, the horizontal part of a stair.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cherished is held dear and prized.

clue.text: A vessel in which to tour Norway

indicators.note: in signals the letters lie inside the words tour Norway, straddling the gap

explanation.surface: A ship is proposed for a cruise around Norway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship for the tour, but it is a container, sitting inside 'tour Norway'.
explanation.definitionFit: An urn is a vase or container, often for ashes.

clue.text: No matter what from a US city

parts.note: NY is New York, the US city

explanation.surface: Anything at all can be had from a city in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Whichever one you like, without restriction, means it does not matter which.

clue.text: It's a question of time

parts.note: the phrase usually means something is bound to happen eventually, but here it describes the question word asking at what time

explanation.walkthrough: 'a question of time' normally means 'inevitable'; read literally, it is the interrogative that asks about time.
explanation.definitionFit: The interrogative used to ask about the moment something happens queries timing.

clue.text: Jack's unusually intent and self-restrained

parts.note: jack is a sailor, AB for able seaman, plus the S of the possessive

indicators.note: unusually means the letters of intent are arranged in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A sailor is strangely determined and keeps himself in check.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack (jack tar) is a sailor, AB; 'unusually' rearranges INTENT to give TINENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who refrains from drink or indulgence practises self-denial and moderation.

clue.text: Muslim leader I married in the morning

parts.note: a.m. means ante meridiem, before noon

explanation.surface: A religious leader says he wed before noon.
explanation.definitionFit: An imam leads prayers in a mosque and guides the congregation.

clue.text: Italian family is in Paris by mid-September

parts.note: est is French for is

indicators.note: mid points to the central letter of the word September

explanation.surface: An Italian dynasty is said to be in the French capital by the middle of September.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is in Paris' means French for 'is', EST; the fifth of September's nine letters is E.
explanation.definitionFit: The Este were a noble dynasty who ruled Ferrara and Modena in Renaissance Italy.

clue.text: To add some colour can take time

parts.note: a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Painting something may take a long while.
explanation.definitionFit: To tint is to colour something lightly, giving it a shade or hue.

clue.text: Manage to become firm by exercise

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
PE is physical education, exercise

explanation.surface: Someone hopes to get fit and steady by working out.
explanation.definitionFit: To cope is to deal successfully with difficulties and get by.

clue.text: Gets in acid specially prepared for making moulds

indicators.note: prepared specially suggests the letters are made into something new, rearranged

parts.note: letters used in the rearrangement

explanation.surface: Something gets dipped into a specially mixed acid during a process of mould making.
explanation.walkthrough: 'specially prepared' rearranges GETS IN ACID.
explanation.definitionFit: Die-casting forces molten metal into steel dies, shaped moulds, to form parts.
